newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Gov. unveils $31 mln flood control plan.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Gov. unveils $31 mln flood control plan.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson unveiled a two-year $31 million plan Friday to rebuild levees and bridges in the state to protect homes and farms from flooding.

Wilson, a Republican, said his plan would increase flood protection, minimize damage from future flooding, and improve the way the state responds to emergencies in the aftermath of California's devastating 1997 floods.

The January storms flooded nearly 300 square miles of land in northern and central California, and forced more than 120,000 people from their homes. More than 24,000 homes and about 2,000 businesses were damaged or destroyed.

Damage to public infrastructure exceeded $1 billion, including damage to highways, levees, sewers and other structures. The floods cost travel businesses and the tourism industry $360 million, the state estimated. Agricultural losses were in excess of $300 million, state officials said.
In response to the widespread flooding, Wilson declared disasters in 48 of California's 58 counties.
Wilson said the state would invest nearly $31 million over the next two years to improve the state's flood control facilities.
In fiscal year 1997-1998, the governor proposed spending $4.4 million to bolster levee inspection and repair efforts in the state, and another $5 million in capital outlay for projects.
